## Location Explorer

The Location Explorer is a collapsible tree view in the Balance Explorer that allows you to navigate through the location groupings for each system and view data related to specific objects. The Location Explorer will show the list of root (pinned) locations and systems (with the preferred system expanded).

- Expanding a system will show all location types within that system.
- Selecting a location and date and clicking the Refresh button will populate the L&U and Members data grids.
- Location types and objects within locations are ordered alphabetically.
- All current members of a given location will display in the Location Explorer; however, the data grid will only display current members within the selected date range.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Object Explorer Search Bar">

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Object Explorer Search Bar">

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Object Explorer Column Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Column Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Object Explorer Column Options">

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options:

- **Sort Ascending** - Sort items in ascending order for the selected column.
- **Sort Descending** - Sort items in descending order for the selected column.
- **Show Column Chooser** - Open the Column Selector to select the columns to display in the grid. (See: [Column Selector](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Resolver/Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector))
- **Best Fit** - Expand the selected column to display the complete contents.
- **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expand all columns to display the complete contents.
- **Filter Editor** - Open the Filter Editor to create conditional statements based on any column or value within the column.

##### Column Order

To change the order of the columns, click a column header and then drag and drop the column to the new location.

You can remove a column by dragging and dropping it outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save this layout when you exit the screen.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sorting">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sorting</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Sorting">

By default, items in a group are sorted by number, in descending order.

<div class="procedure">

To change the sort order:

- Click any column header to sort items by that parameter.
- Click a header again to reverse the list order (ascending or descending).
- Right-click a column header and select **Sort Ascending** or **Sort Descending**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Object Explorer Filtering Objects">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Filtering</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Object Explorer Filtering Objects">

You can filter items by a single column or by multiple columns.

<div class="procedure">

To filter by a single column:

1.  Hover over a column header to display the filter icon.
2.  Click the filter icon to open the Filter dialog box. The dialog box contains two tabs:
    - **Filter Values** - Select the values that you want to display.
    - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example: "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). Select the condition, and then specify a value.
3.  Close the Filter dialog box by clicking on the grid.
4.  After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter.

To filter by multiple columns, right-click a column header and select **Filter Editor**.

</div>
